subject: [PATCH v8 0/7] mm/page_counter: move stock from mem_cgroup to page_counter

reviews.author: Balbir Singh
reviews.summary: Reviewer questioned the primary motivation behind moving stock from mem_cgroup to page_counter and asked for examples of new page_counters that would be added.
reviews.raw_body:
Is the main motivation ease of addition of page_counters to a memcg?
What would those counters be, why not add them here?

Balbir

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed Balbir's concern about the motivation for adding new page_counters, explaining that they are intended to track per-tier per-memcg residence and would not make sense without the enforcement parts. The author provided a link to their tiered memcg series for additional context.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Balbir,

Thank you for your interest in the series! So yes, that is the main
motivation but this series offers standalone benefits as well (which
are right above).

The new page_counters that I want to add track per-tier per-memcg
residence. Those are used for enforcement (and not necessarily for
visibility), so I think they wouldn't make too much sense to add on
their own now, without the actual enforcement parts.

What do you think? I've also linked my tiered memcg series [1] if you
wanted additional context.

Thank you, I hope you have a great day!
Joshua

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260807202059.2620949-1-joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com/

2026-11-05.patch_summary: This patch series moves the stock implementation from memcontrol to page_counter, allowing for better separation of charge caching and policy management. The stock is a per-CPU cache of precharged pages that speeds up small allocations by avoiding frequent walks of the page_counter hierarchy. By moving it to page_counter, the patch simplifies the handling of stock in non-leaf cgroups and prepares for future improvements. It also ensures that locking behavior remains unchanged and that exact charging is preserved for non-spinning callers.
